at komme forbi.explanation: "At komme forbi" means "to come by". To invite someone to drop in for a visit, say: "Kom forbi i aften" (Come by tonight). To say you cannot pass something in the way, use it for "get past": "Vi kan ikke komme forbi bilen" (We cannot get past the car).

at komme frem.explanation: "At komme frem" means "to arrive / come forward". To say when a trip ended, say: "Vi kom frem klokken seks" (We arrived at six o'clock). To say someone stepped forward, say: "Han kom frem fra mængden" (He came forward from the crowd).

at komme godt ud af det med.explanation: "At komme godt ud af det med" means "to get along with". To say you have a good relationship with someone, say: "Jeg kommer godt ud af det med min chef" (I get along well with my boss). Put "dårligt" (badly) in place of "godt" (well) to say the opposite: "Jeg kommer dårligt ud af det med min nabo" (I get along badly with my neighbor).

at komme hjem.explanation: "At komme hjem" means "to come home". To ask when someone gets home, say: "Hvornår kommer du hjem?" (When will you get home?). To say you are setting off for home, use "at tage hjem" (to go home): "Jeg tager hjem nu" (I am going home now).

at komme i gang.explanation: "At komme i gang" means "to get started". To name the task you start, add "med" (with) and the task: "Jeg kom i gang med opgaven" (I got started on the task).

at komme i tanke om.explanation: "At komme i tanke om" means "to remember / think of". To say a thing suddenly came back to you, say: "Jeg kom i tanke om nøglerne" (I remembered the keys). To say you simply keep something in memory, use "at huske" (to remember): "Jeg husker hans navn" (I remember his name).

at komme ind.explanation: "At komme ind" means "to come in". To invite someone into a room, say: "Kom ind!" (Come in!). To say you could not get into a place, say: "Vi kom ikke ind i klubben" (We could not get into the club).

at komme med.explanation: "At komme med" means "to come along / bring". To ask if someone joins you, say: "Kommer du med?" (Are you coming along?). To say someone brought something, say: "Hun kom med kage" (She brought cake).

at komme ned.explanation: "At komme ned" means "to come down". To tell someone to come down from a high place, say: "Kom ned derfra!" (Come down from there!).

at komme op.explanation: "At komme op" means "to come up / get up". To invite someone upstairs, say: "Kom op til os!" (Come up to us!). To push someone to try harder, say: "Kom op!" (Come on!). To get out of bed, use "at stå op" (to get up): "Jeg står op klokken syv" (I get up at seven).

at komme over.explanation: "At komme over" means "to get over". To say someone never recovered from something hard, say: "Han kom aldrig over det" (He never got over it). To invite someone to visit you, say: "Kom over til os!" (Come over to our place!).

at komme sig.explanation: "At komme sig" means "to recover". It is built from "at komme" (to come) and "sig" (oneself). To name what you recover from, add "efter" (after): "Jeg kommer mig efter sygdommen" (I am recovering from the illness).

at komme til skade.explanation: "At komme til skade" means "to get hurt". To say when someone got hurt, say: "Han kom til skade i går" (He got hurt yesterday). To name the body part, add "på" (on) before it: "Jeg kom til skade på benet" (I hurt my leg).

at komme tilbage.explanation: "At komme tilbage" means "to come back". To say you will return soon, say: "Jeg kommer snart tilbage" (I will be back soon). The word "tilbage" (back) is also in "at give tilbage" (to give back) and "at betale tilbage" (to pay back).

at komme ud.explanation: "At komme ud" means "to come out / get out". To tell someone to leave a room, say: "Kom ud!" (Come out!). To say where someone comes out of, add "af" (of): "Han kommer ud af skolen" (He comes out of the school).

at komme videre.explanation: "At komme videre" means "to move on". To say you want to leave something painful behind, say: "Jeg vil gerne komme videre efter bruddet" (I want to move on after the breakup). To say you continue a trip, say: "Vi kom videre til næste by" (We went on to the next town).

at kommentere.explanation: "At kommentere" means "to comment". To say what you comment on, put it right after the verb, with no word for "on": "Hun kommenterer videoen" (She is commenting on the video).

at kommunikere.explanation: "At kommunikere" means "to communicate". To say which language you use, add "på" (in): "Vi kommunikerer på dansk" (We communicate in Danish). To name the person you communicate with, add "med" (with): "Jeg kommunikerer med kunden" (I communicate with the customer).

at kompensere.explanation: "At kompensere" means "to compensate". To name what you make up for, add "for" (for) before it: "Jeg kompenserer for fejlen" (I compensate for the mistake).

at komplicere.explanation: "At komplicere" means "to complicate". To say something makes matters harder, add "tingene" (the things): "Det komplicerer tingene" (That complicates things).

at komponere.explanation: "At komponere" means "to compose". To say who writes the music and who plays it, say: "Hun komponerer, og han spiller" (She composes and he plays).

at koncentrere sig.explanation: "At koncentrere sig" means "to concentrate". To say you cannot focus, say: "Jeg kan ikke koncentrere mig" (I cannot concentrate). To name the task you focus on, add "om" (on) before the task: "Vi koncentrerer os om opgaven" (We are concentrating on the task).

at konfirmere.explanation: "At konfirmere" means "to confirm", in the church ceremony where a young person confirms their baptism. In Denmark, the confirmation is followed by a family party called "en konfirmationsfest". To say you have been confirmed, say: "Jeg er konfirmeret" (I am confirmed).

at konkludere.explanation: "At konkludere" means "to conclude". To state the conclusion, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg konkluderer, at planen virker" (I conclude that the plan works).

at konkurrere.explanation: "At konkurrere" means "to compete". To say who you compete with, add "med" (with): "Jeg konkurrerer med min bror" (I compete with my brother). To name the prize, add "om" (for): "Vi konkurrerer om prisen" (We compete for the prize).
